camarillasaurus:eswiki:3.title: Camarillasaurus cirugedae (Relación con Camarillas y Pedro Cirugeda Buj)

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) in what is now northeastern Spain.
facts.quote: Camarillasaurus (meaning "Camarillas lizard") is an extinct genus of spinosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous period (Barremian) of Camarillas, Teruel Province, in what is now northeastern Spain.

facts.statement: Fossils of Camarillasaurus were discovered in the Camarillas Formation.
facts.quote: Fossils of Camarillasaurus were discovered in the Camarillas Formation.

facts.statement: A 2024 study recovered Camarillasaurus within the Spinosauridae, either as the basalmost spinosaurine or as a basal spinosaurid sister to Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: In the 2024 description of the Iberian spinosaurid Riojavenatrix by Isasmendi et al., Camarillasaurus was once again recovered in the Spinosauridae, either as the basalmost spinosaurine or a basal spinosaurid as the sister to Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae.

facts.statement: In 2025, Rauhut and colleagues found high support for placing Camarillasaurus within Spinosaurinae as the sister taxon to a clade containing Spinosaurus and a Kem Kem spinosaurid.
facts.quote: In 2025, Rauhut and colleagues reassessed the anatomy and phylogenetic position of Camarillasaurus, finding high support for its placement within Spinosaurinae, as the sister taxon to a clade consisting of Spinosaurus and Kem Kem spinosaurid (FSAC-KK 11888; possibly Spinosaurus).

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus is classified in the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus is classified in the subfamily Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Spinosaurinae

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus was of medium size, approximately 4 meters long, with a relatively slender build.
facts.quote: Camarillasaurus era de tamaño medio, alrededor de los 4 metros de largo y con una complexión relativamente delgada.

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus is known from fragmentary remains including a tooth, a possible cervical vertebra, two sternal plates, the proximal part of a right tibia, a broken right scapulocoracoid, an incomplete sacrum, five caudal vertebrae, a caudal neural arch, a chevron, an almost complete presacral rib, and various bone fragments.
facts.quote: Se conoce a través de los restos fragmentarios que comprenden un diente, una posible vértebra cervical dos placas esternales, la parte proximal de una tibia derecha, un escapulocoracoide derecho roto, el sacro incompleto, cinco vértebras caudales, un arco neural caudal, un cheurón, una costilla presacral casi completa y algunos fragmentos de vértebras, costillas y otros huesos.

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus was likely a bipedal predator with long hind legs, distinguished by two autapomorphies: a highly developed cnemial crest making the distal tibia extremely deep, and a deep longitudinal groove in the tibia.
facts.quote: Camarillasaurus era probablemente un depredador bípedo con largas patas traseras, y se diferencia de otros animales similares como Elaphrosaurus debido a dos autapomorfías, características derivadas, el gran desarrollo de la zona de cresta cnemial, llevando la parte distal de la tibia a ser extremadamente profunda y la presencia de una ranura longitudinal de profundidad en la tibia.

facts.statement: Since its initial description in 2012, Camarillasaurus was interpreted as a basal ceratosaur, serving as a key representative for understanding early diversity and evolution of this group in Laurasia during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Desde su descripción inicial en 2012, el taxón fue interpretado como un ceratosaurio basal, lo que lo situaba como un representante clave para comprender la diversidad y evolución temprana de este grupo en Laurasia durante el Cretácico Inferior.

facts.statement: Subsequent studies proposed including Camarillasaurus within the Spinosauridae, modifying its scientific relevance by integrating it into the context of spinosaurid radiation in Europe.
facts.quote: Posteriormente, estudios posteriores propusieron su inclusión dentro de la familia Spinosauridae, lo que ha modificado su relevancia científica al integrarlo en el contexto de la radiación de los espinosáuridos en Europa.

facts.statement: Due to fragmentary fossil material and differing phylogenetic interpretations, Camarillasaurus remains a reference taxon in debates regarding the evolution of European Early Cretaceous theropods and the presence and diversity of spinosaurids in Western Europe.
facts.quote: En cualquier caso, la fragmentariedad del material fósil y las diferentes interpretaciones filogenéticas hacen de Camarillasaurus un taxón de referencia en los debates sobre la evolución de los terópodos europeos del Cretácico Inferior, así como en la discusión sobre la presencia y diversidad de espinosáuridos en Europa occidental.

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus was first described in 2012 based on fossils found in the Camarillas Formation in Camarillas, Teruel Province, Spain.
facts.quote: Camarillasaurus fue descrito por primera vez en 2012, basado en restos fósiles encontrados en la Formación Camarillas en Camarillas, Provincia de Teruel, España.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was initially classified as a ceratosaurian, phylogenetically near the base of the clade and perhaps more derived than the Chinese Limusaurus.
facts.quote: El nuevo dinosaurio fue clasificado como un ceratosauriano, filogenéticamente cerca de la base del clado, y tal vez más derivado que el Limusaurus chino.

facts.statement: In a 2019 EAVP conference summary, Oliver Rauhut and colleagues suggested it was instead a member of the Spinosauridae family rather than a ceratosaurian.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en un resumen de la conferencia de 2019 de la EAVP, Oliver Rauhut y colaboradores sugirieron que era en cambio un miembro de la familia Spinosauridae en lugar de ser un ceratosaurio

facts.statement: A 2021 formal publication by Samathi supported the conclusion that Camarillasaurus is similar to Thai spinosaurid materials and other family taxa.
facts.quote: En 2021, el capítulo fue publicado formalmente como un artículo científico, con la misma conclusión; Samathi señaló las similitudes con los materiales de espinosáuridos de Tailandia y con otros taxones de la familia.

facts.statement: A 2025 extensive review by Rauhut and colleagues reclassified Camarillasaurus as a spinosaurine, based on new material recovered in 2018 including the surangular/articular, part of a mid-caudal vertebra, the femur, a foot ungual phalanx, and part of a tooth.
facts.quote: En 2025, Rauhut y colaboradores publicaron una revisión extensa del material de Camarillasaurus, incluyendo nuevo material recuperado en el yacimiento tipo durante 2018, incluyendo el surangular/articular, parte de una vértebra caudal media, el fémur, una falange ungual del pie y parte de un diente-.

facts.statement: The parent group of Camarillasaurus is Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Spinosaurinae

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus belongs to the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Camarillasaurus lived during the Barremian stage, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Camarillasaurus is Camarillasaurus cirugedae.
facts.quote: Type species: Camarillasaurus cirugedae

rejected.quote: Described in 2014, it was originally identified as a ceratosaurian theropod, but later studies suggested affinities to the Spinosauridae.

rejected.quote: However, in an abstract presented at the 2019 conference of the European Association of Vertebrate Palaeontologists, Oliver Rauhut and colleagues suggested it was more likely to be a member of the Megalosauroidea—likely the Spinosauridae—rather than a ceratosaur, based on characters of the posterior caudal vertebrae and newly excavated material at the type locality.

rejected.statement: The 2025 study recovered Camarillasaurus as a spinosaurine spinosaurid alongside other Iberian taxa, suggesting the absence of baryonic spinosaurids in the Iberian Peninsula.
rejected.quote: El nuevo estudio recupera a Camarillasaurus como un esponosaurio espinosaurino, junto con el resto de taxones ibéricos, sugiriendo la ausencia de espinosaurios barioniquinos en la península ibérica.
